section_job.evidence: The draft performs exactly the job in section_job: it opens by comparing user-side data needs against the 260-dataset catalog (para 1-2), states the 11 structural gaps with one-sentence definitions (list, lines 7-17), states per-service obstacles for all 9 services (list, lines 21-29), states the 75-topic website-content readiness split (lines 33-37), and closes with a transition to A-BTR (lines 39-41) without developing the A-BTR argument itself. audience_decision_value.evidence: Every list item is framed around what a DCCE executive needs to know to sequence development (e.g. line 21: certification gap 'is the precondition for data-rights decisions'; line 31: 'lets the next development phase prioritize according to each service's actual gap obligations'). The draft foregrounds findings and consequences, not the consultant's data-collection workflow -- the one process mention (line 5, interviews/workshop/survey) is a single clause establishing evidence basis, not a workflow narrative.

evidence_payload.evidence: Each of the three governing-thought threads carries claim + concrete evidence + consequence: the 11-gap list (lines 7-17) gives a one-sentence mechanism per gap; the per-service list (lines 21-29) names the specific blocking gap numbers and the mechanism for each of the 9 services; the content-readiness paragraph (lines 33-39) gives the 16/26/33-topic breakdown against the 391-item inventory and states the 79% consequence. causal_logic.evidence: Causal chains run forward without reversal: demand-vs-supply comparison produces the 11 gaps (lines 3-17) -> the 11 gaps combine differently to block each service (lines 19-29) -> the content-readiness figure is stated as an independent, whole-website fact (lines 33-39) -> the closing paragraph (39-41) correctly identifies all three as facets of one technical problem and uses A-BTR's recurring, mandatory nature as the reason to sequence it first, which is the same causal chain the map's arg-04 warrant specifies.

argument_fidelity.evidence: All 4 map units surface: arg-01's 11 gaps appear with definitions drawn faithfully from its grounds (spot-checked all 11 against arg-01 grounds text -- gap 9's certification/stewardship/refusal-process triad, gap 10's 'distinct from gap 8' framing, and gap 11's policy-vs-data framing all match; gap 2 compresses out the grounds' aside about 5km downscaled climate data closing the climate-driver end, which is expected altitude-driven simplification, not drift, since the map's application_to_design calls for one-to-two sentences per gap). arg-02's 9 services and their exact blocking-gap-number combinations (lines 21-29) match the grounds' per-service list one-to-one, including the two flagged as 'this service depends on gap 10 more than any other' (service 3) and 'least developed service' (service 6). arg-03's 16/26/33/391/75/79% figures (lines 33-39) match exactly, and the draft states the whole-website scope caveat the warrant calls for. arg-04's closing (lines 39-41) states the 'one technical problem, not three' synthesis and the A-BTR-first sequencing with the reason (binding, recurring, draws on multiple gaps) that the warrant specifies. No claim in the draft is unsupported by the map, and no map unit is dropped.

The two English parentheticals flagged by the linter (NCAIF full name, A-BTR full name) are standard first-mention glosses, not artifact leakage.

findings.location: Structural-gap list, item 11 (line 17): "ช่องว่างบางส่วนไม่ได้รอข้อมูลหรือการวิเคราะห์เพิ่มเติม แต่รอการตัดสินใจเชิงนโยบายหรือเชิงสถาบันเพื่อกำหนดทิศทางต่อไป"
findings.issue: This sentence uses the literal 'ไม่ได้...แต่...' negation-contrast scaffold flagged as an AI-tell pattern to watch for beyond the linter's 3 regex checks. The content is faithful to arg-01's grounds definition of gap 11 ('close on a policy or institutional decision rather than new data or analysis') and is a factual classification rather than a justify-by-flaw rhetorical move, but the surface structure matches the banned negate-then-affirm-with-'แต่' shape the contract's report_specific_rules prohibits ('ไม่ใช่...แต่...' family).
findings.disposition: Content is faithful and the meaning is unchanged; recommend rephrasing to an affirmative lead (e.g. 'ช่องว่างบางส่วนรอการตัดสินใจเชิงนโยบายหรือเชิงสถาบันเพื่อกำหนดทิศทางต่อไป มากกว่าจะรอข้อมูลหรือการวิเคราะห์เพิ่มเติม') in a future pass, but this is a local stylistic defect that does not change the governing meaning. Accepted for human review rather than blocking this pass.

findings.location: Paragraph 1, first mention of the NCAIF framework (line 3): "...(National Climate Adaptation Information Framework) ซึ่งต่อไปเรียกว่า..."
findings.issue: The contract's terminology rule gives an exact first-mention template that includes the ': NCAIF' abbreviation inside the parenthetical ('(National Climate Adaptation Information Framework: NCAIF)'). The draft omits ': NCAIF' from the parenthetical. This does not violate the rule's core intent -- 'never bare English NCAIF' -- because the bare acronym 'NCAIF' never appears anywhere in the draft, satisfied by omission rather than by the specified exact phrasing.
findings.disposition: Local formatting deviation from the contract's literal example text; does not create the bare-acronym problem the rule exists to prevent and does not affect meaning or reader comprehension. Accepted for human review rather than blocking this pass.
